identification: Strapped pack (2 steel straps, on 2 bearers) of new, unfinished, light-coloured Tasmanian oak (eucalypt) tongue-and-groove flooring, catalogued 85 x 20 mm (boards in photo 2 look about 80-85 mm cover, consistent). Pack about 2.4 m long overall; boards of mixed lengths from short offcuts (roughly 0.5 m) up to about 2.4 m, many boards visibly end-matched (tongue on the end). Hand-marked on a board: 'APPROX 11.00 m/2 TAS OAK T+G' with a yellow circled '6' (pack number). Clean, no visible water staining; some boards with gum veins/knots typical of standard/feature grade.

viewing_check: Measure board cover width and thickness; count layers x boards across and estimate average length to check the m2 claim; pull a few boards from the middle to see the share of short (<60 cm) offcuts; check for end-matching, splits, borer, moisture staining and mixed species; note how you'd move it (ute/trailer, roughly 250-400 kg).
